c.tagline: River meets ocean at Africa's smallest mainland capital.

taxi.fareNote: Tourist taxis (green) charge fixed negotiated fares set by tourism board tariffs; yellow-yellow local shared taxis are cheaper but follow fixed routes rather than meters. Always agree the fare before departure as meters are not used.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; many hotels and resorts keep private clinic contacts and expats often rely on Medicare/Westfield or Kairaba clinics in Kotu/Fajara for faster service.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The historic colonial-era capital on St Mary's Island itself, with faded colonial architecture, Albert Market, and government buildings; few tourists actually sleep here, suiting history buffs and those wanting an authentic, non-touristy base near the ferry terminal.

The Gambia's main beach resort strip with Kololi, Senegambia and Bijilo blending together; big all-inclusive resorts, nightlife, restaurants and craft markets, suiting first-time visitors and package travelers who want beach plus amenities in one place.

A quieter beachfront area with a mix of package hotels and self-catering apartments just north of Kololi, popular with British and European charter tourists and families wanting a calmer beach scene with easy access to Senegambia's nightlife.

An upscale, leafy residential and diplomatic area near the coast with boutique lodges, embassies and golf course, suiting travelers wanting a quieter, more refined stay close to the beach and Cape Point.

A fishing village atmosphere at the northern tip of the peninsula where the river meets the Atlantic, home to a monkey sanctuary and craft markets, suiting travelers who want a laid-back, semi-local coastal vibe.

water.note: Tap water is not safe; use sealed bottled water only.

transit.pay: Pay cash in dalasi directly to the driver or conductor on boarding for buses and bush taxis; fares for shared routes are fixed per seat and posted at motor parks. The Banjul-Barra ferry sells paper tickets at the terminal for foot passengers and vehicles.
transit.hours: Bush taxis and gelly-gellys run roughly 6am-8pm with no fixed schedule (depart when full); GTSC buses run limited daytime schedules; the Banjul-Barra ferry operates several crossings daily but with unpredictable delays and no reliable night service.
transit.note: There is no formal urban transit network; public transport is dominated by informal shared taxis and minibuses, and most visitors rely on hotel transfers or negotiated taxis instead.

bus: private minivan/gelly-gelly bush taxis between Banjul, Serekunda and Kombo coastal towns
ferry: Banjul-Barra Ferry across the River Gambia

airport.name: Banjul International Airport (BJL)
rentals: local operators (Sannoh Car Rentals, Gambia Car Hire)

transit.m: shared/bush taxi to Serekunda then local transport

tip.r: Not obligatory but appreciated in resorts and restaurants; rounding up or 10% is common for good service, especially where a service charge isn't already included.
